 VP Sara blasts graft as trial forges on
 EO Lisa Marie Apacible and Edjen Oliquino · 19 November 2026 · 12:17 AM PHT · 3 MIN READ 
 VICE President Sara Duterte
 Text size A− Reset A+ Save Vice President Sara Duterte described corruption in government as deeply entrenched, depriving Filipinos of economic opportunities and hampering the country’s development, a day before the impeachment trial resumes that may result in her ouster. 
 In a social media post on her participation in the 52nd Philippine Business Conference and Expo, she urged Filipinos to demand accountability from public officials.
 Duterte, without naming anyone, said corruption remained a major obstacle to the country’s aspiration for a better future.

 Edjen Oliquino · 18 November 2026 
 “It is a progressive disorder that has embedded itself deep within the DNA of the government, and tragically, it is the Filipino people who are left to suffer the consequences,” she said.
 Duterte said Filipinos shared a common aspiration for a future where everyone could live with dignity, security, and hope, but corruption continued to stand in the way of achieving this.
 She also called on the citizens to take responsibility for nation-building.
 “As citizens, we have responsibilities too — to obey the law, reject corruption, protect our communities, participate in our democracy, and demand accountability from those who govern us,” she said.
 “Nation-building is a shared responsibility,” she added.
 Also read Ilocos tobacco windfall tests accountability 
 Compelling evidence needed
 As Duterte’s impeachment trial is set to resume and is expected to produce a verdict soon, Senator Alan Cayetano reiterated on Wednesday that the evidence against her must be compelling enough to secure a unanimous acquittal or conviction.
 Otherwise, he warned a vague outcome could further divide the country and stoke public outrage amid unresolved issues, such as the flood control scandal, economic instability, and anomalous insertions in the national budget.
 “This problem coincides with the national budget,” the minority leader told reporters on the sidelines of the 51st Philippine National Prayer Breakfast. 
 “Whether we accept it or not, we’re a nation in crisis. We have an identity crisis, a crisis in relationships with each other, with trust in government — we have a corruption crisis,” he said. 
 His remarks came as the Senate prepares to resume the impeachment trial today, following a three-day suspension for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits hosted by the Philippines. 
 The trial is entering its final stretch, with the defense intending to present eight to 10 more witnesses. 
 Duterte’s camp initially requested 30 trial days, but after the prosecution dropped three charges — leaving only Article 2 — this was trimmed to 10 days, with three already exhausted last week. 
 The defense subpoenaed four witnesses for Thursday and Friday, aiming to disprove allegations of unexplained wealth and undeclared assets in Duterte’s SALN, in violation of the Constitution. 
 Unexplained wealth explained
 Earlier, a prosecution witness, lawyer Alexander Cabrera, showed the impeachment court his forensic financial report alleging that Duterte had P817.87 million in unexplained wealth and income accumulated between 2022 and 2025. 
 His findings also showed that Gencorp Industries Inc. — a firm partly owned by Duterte’s husband, Atty. Mans Carpio — had not declared its revenue of P1.04 billion to the Bureau of Internal Revenue from 2022 to 2025. The period overlapped with Duterte’s tenure as Vice President.
 The House of Representatives twice impeached Duterte, who was accused of betrayal of public trust, culpable violation of the Constitution, graft and corruption, among others.
 Impeachment court Presiding Officer Senator Chiz Escudero maintained that the court had no fixed timeline. He, however, was hopeful the trial would wrap up by December.
 Impeachment court spokesperson Atty. Reginald Tongol said it would take almost a month from when the defense rests its case until the senator-judges decide whether to convict or acquit the VP for alleged unexplained wealth and remove her from office.
